svg.title: One Order, One Evidence Trail, One Settlement
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-order-to-cash-dispatch; chart type: process_flow; title: One Order, One Evidence Trail, One Settlement; subtitle: Separate passenger transport and specimen handling within one dispatch desk.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The pod coordinates contracted providers rather than owning a fleet. Passenger trips and specimen movements require separate service rules, escalation procedures, and evidence packets.; caption: Close each assignment only after reconciling authorization, performance evidence, payer billing, and provider settlement.; stages: label: Validate the contracted order; value: Confirm payer, service scope, authorization, and collection terms; numeric value: 1.0; detail: For NEMT, verify member eligibility, authorized transport level, destination, and standing-order validity. For courier work, verify specimen class, receiving hours, packaging responsibility, and contracted pickup deadline.; label: Match qualified transport capacity; value: Assign an eligible provider with documented backup coverage; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Check driver credentials, vehicle suitability, insurance, service-area limits, and exclusions. A signed owner-operator agreement does not resolve worker classification.; label: Dispatch and capture service events; value: Record timestamped pickup, movement, delivery, and exceptions; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use RouteGenie or MediRoutes for configured NEMT GPS events. Use barcode custody records for specimens; escalate missed STAT pickups to the named laboratory contact immediately.; label: Build the payer evidence packet; value: Reconcile ordered service against completed service before billing; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Scrub 837P claims only where the payer requires that format; otherwise submit the contracted broker file or courier invoice. Attach required trip verification or custody evidence.; label: Collect, settle, and reconcile; value: Track receivables separately from provider payment obligations; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Forecast Medicaid broker Net-30/45 collection exposure against settlement dates. Under the canonical model, 55% of gross billings funds drivers and 45% remains before pod costs and owner profit.
